## D — Accuracy notes and source flags: backing, parking, passenger restraints, crashes, insurance and phones
Every C and C2 fact cites exactly one physical manual page from the selected range; nothing relies on outside knowledge.
The hill parking and parallel parking panels were read from their extracted captions; the dossier states the wheel directions and steps exactly as captioned and adds nothing drawn only in the pictures [A02].
The forward-facing seat limit is printed as a typical weight range that depends on the manufacturer; the dossier keeps it as typical, not as a legal threshold [A04].
The cell phone paragraph covers composing, reading or sending messages and internet access, with emergency, crash-reporting and hands-free exceptions; the dossier does not extend it to any calling rule the page does not print [A06] (verify MN-TRAFFICB-D-PHONE).
Seat belt and airbag points also appear in the vehicle chapter; the facts here are restated from this chapter's own pages in fresh wording and cite only these pages.
Fees and fines are stated exactly as printed and are isolated as dynamic facts in part C.

corpus_stability.reason: The Minnesota Driver’s Manual prints a single edition line (June 2026) on its front cover and opens with a New laws and information chapter that collects recent changes in one place, with no sign of more than one rewrite per year in the selected pages.

verification_debt.claim_text: On physical page 43 the Minnesota Driver's Manual (June 2026) limits its cell phone rule to composing, reading or sending electronic messages and internet access, with voice-activated or hands-free use listed as an exception; confirm against an official DPS or DVS source whether written test items cover any further wireless device rule.
